title: Theoretical Limits of Language Model Alignment

Despite their widespread use, the fundamental limits of reward improvement under a KL budget remain poorly understood. title: Read Less, Solve More: Token-Efficient Sparse Reading of External Content for AI Agents
excerpt: Web-facing AI agents repeatedly access webpages, documents, repositories, and tool responses, yet reading interfaces often expose entire objects when only sparse evidence is needed. Its Read Intent Protocol tracks evolving needs and source coverage; Adaptive Reader Backends select how evidence is located and exposed; and the Budgeted Read Gate bounds cumulative raw exposure per episode with faithful full-view fallback. A unified Reader interface supports interchangeable evidence…

ai.summary: The paper introduces SparseRead, a reading control layer for AI agents that uses a Read Intent Protocol and Adaptive Reader Backends to selectively ingest only needed parts of webpages, documents, or tool responses, reducing token usage and latency without changing the agent model.
ai.why: It can lower costs and speed up agent pipelines, useful for developers building web‑enabled AI assistants.

title: SteerDistill: Quantizing LLM Agents via Closed-Loop Teacher Steering
excerpt: Low-bit quantization reduces the inference cost of LLM agents but can compromise task success. Examining failed rollouts, we find that quantized agents overlook task requirements or environmental conditions, producing environment transitions that diverge from successful full-precision references. Correcting these behavioral divergences remains difficult: offline data may miss the student's failure contexts, while its own rollouts may provide few correct responses in those contexts. We introduce SteerDistill, a quantization-aware distillation method in which a full-precision teacher guides the student to revise failed responses and iteratively refines its guidance using feedback from student…

ai.summary: SteerDistill proposes a closed‑loop teacher‑steering method to quantize LLM agents to low‑bit precision while preserving task success by correcting behavioral divergences that appear after quantization.
ai.why: Enables cheaper inference for LLM‑based agents without sacrificing performance, useful for edge deployment.

title: FAME-QP: A GPU-Accelerated Quadratic-Programming Solver for Real-Time Model Predictive Control
excerpt: We present FAME-QP, a GPU-accelerated solver for dense quadratic programs arising in linear model predictive control. FAME-QP combines constraint-dependent operator representations with fused single- and two-kernel iterations replayed through CUDA graphs, automatically selecting the execution configuration through device calibration and problem-specific timing. It probes a cached operator bank to select the initial penalty and updates operators lazily when problem matrices change. Numerical benchmarks and simulated humanoid and quadrotor control experiments demonstrate reduced latency relative to competing GPU solvers while maintaining solution accuracy and control performance.

ai.summary: FAME‑QP is a GPU‑accelerated quadratic‑programming solver for dense QPs in linear model predictive control, using CUDA graphs and operator caching to auto‑tune execution and reduce latency.
ai.why: Developers building real‑time control systems can integrate FAME‑QP to achieve faster MPC computations on GPUs.

title: Subliminal Learning in Vision-Language Models
